features.title: Business tools for everyday shop operations
features.description: Explore DukaanSet billing, inventory, customer credit, purchases and daily business workflows, with clear implementation boundaries.
features.headline:
The essentials,
working together.
features.intro: A bill is more than a number. It changes the shelf, the customer’s balance and the picture of your day. DukaanSet keeps those everyday records connected.

sections.title: Start with a sale
sections.body: Search the product catalogue, add quantities and record how the customer paid. Confirming the bill records its stock movement and balance together.
items: Cash, UPI and customer credit records
Partial payment with a named customer

sections.title: Follow your stock
sections.body: Opening stock, purchases, sales and manual adjustments all have a reason. The inventory ledger helps you understand what changed instead of only seeing a current quantity.

sections.title: Make the day understandable
sections.body: Review sales, collected payments, outstanding balances and tasks. Close the day with the figures your records actually support.

sections.title: Know what is still ahead
sections.body: External payment collection, automatic messages, official e-invoicing, advanced variants and fully offline financial transactions need dedicated integration and validation. The interface should always tell you when a service is unavailable.

features/billing.title: Connected billing for small shops
features/billing.description: Create itemised shop bills with connected stock and customer payment records in DukaanSet. Understand partial payments and invoice limitations.
features/billing.headline:
A bill made.
A day kept in order.
features/billing.intro: Find the products, add the quantities and record the payment. The sale, its stock deduction and any unpaid customer amount belong in one connected transaction.

sections.title: An everyday sale, step by step
sections.body: Start a new bill from the app. Search by product name, check its unit and add the quantity sold. Review the items and total before confirming.
items: The server validates quantities and stock
Prices are snapshotted into the invoice
Confirmed bills are retained for history

sections.title: When a customer pays part now
sections.body: Attach the bill to a customer and enter the amount received. The remainder becomes that customer’s outstanding credit. Record later repayments against the same business to keep their balance traceable.
items: A named customer is required for credit
The received amount cannot exceed the bill
The total and amount due are shown separately

sections.title: An invoice is a record
sections.body: An invoice can be opened and printed from the browser. Ordinary invoice creation does not mean government-verified GST e-invoicing. No IRN, GST portal submission or tax-compliance certification is provided.

sections.title: A connection is required
sections.body: This release confirms invoices online. If saving fails, the app surfaces the error; it must not show a successful bill or reduce stock for a transaction that has not been committed.

features/inventory.title: Inventory and stock movement tracking
features/inventory.description: Track products, opening stock, sales, purchases and reviewed voice or manual stock receipts, with low-stock and product-expiry attention in DukaanSet.
features/inventory.headline:
Know what you have.
See what changed.
features/inventory.intro: Stock should tell a story: what came in, what sold and what needs a second look. Follow your quantities in the units your business actually uses.

sections.title: Start with a useful catalogue
sections.body: Add a product name, selling price, cost, unit and opening quantity. Edit prices and aliases later. Minimum-stock levels and product expiry dates help highlight items that need attention.
items: Pieces and packs for everyday items
Kilograms and decimal quantities for produce
Metres for hardware and electrical stock

sections.title: Movement, with a reason
sections.body: Sales deduct stock, purchase receipts add stock and manual adjustments record an explicit reason. These movements remain separate from the current quantity so a business owner can review the history.

sections.title: Speak, review, then receive stock
sections.body: Supported browsers can capture a stock command after you enable the microphone. Review the matched products, units and quantities before confirming. Type or enter items manually when speech is unavailable or inaccurate. No remote speech or AI provider is connected by this application.

sections.title: Use compatible units and configured packs
sections.body: Stock receipts support gram/kilogram and millilitre/litre conversions. A saved pack size allows a box or pack receipt to become the product's base quantity; an unknown pack size is rejected. Advanced selling conversion matrices are a later phase.

sections.title: Restock with context
sections.body: Low-stock views point you back to the product. Review what remains, then record an actual supplier purchase when stock arrives. Suggested attention is not an automatically placed order.

sections.title: Specialised inventory is phased
sections.body: Product-level expiry attention is available. Batch-specific expiry, full size and colour matrices, serial numbers, advanced selling conversions and warranty workflows still need dedicated implementation and tests.

features/udhar.title: Customer credit and payment tracking
features/udhar.description: Keep customer udhaar and partial payments understandable with connected invoices, repayments and business-specific balances in DukaanSet.
features/udhar.headline:
Remember the customer.
Let the records remember the rest.
features/udhar.intro: Some customers pay now. Some pay later. See outstanding amounts alongside the bills and payments that explain them.

sections.title: Give every balance a customer
sections.body: Create a customer record with a name and optional contact information. A sale on credit must be linked to a customer, so the unpaid amount does not become an unexplained shop total.

sections.title: Keep partial payments simple
sections.body: A ₹1,000 bill with ₹600 received leaves ₹400 due. The sale remains ₹1,000; cash collected remains ₹600. DukaanSet separates those concepts so you can read the day correctly.
items: Invoice amount and payment amount stay distinct
A payment cannot be larger than the balance due

sections.title: Review the relationship
sections.body: Open a customer’s history to see their transactions and current balance. Use business records rather than memory to discuss what remains unpaid.

sections.title: Messages stay in your control
sections.body: Automatic WhatsApp, SMS and payment reminders are not active without a provider and consent workflow. The app does not silently send messages or collect customer payments.

features/ai.title: Read-only AI assistance and availability
features/ai.description: Recorded-data summaries and an optional configured read-only AI adapter, with explicit business permissions and live provider limits.
features/ai.headline:
Ask a better question
about your business.
features/ai.intro: The AI direction is practical: explain an authorised business summary, surface relevant stock attention and help a merchant understand the records. It must stay grounded in the data.
features/ai.note: The optional read-only adapter requires provider credentials and live validation. Homepage answers are illustrative examples.

sections.title: Questions worth helping with
sections.body: The proposed assistant can help explain today’s sales, outstanding customer balances or products below minimum stock. A useful answer should cite the underlying business summary instead of inventing a recommendation.
items: Which products are low in stock?
How much customer credit remains unpaid?

sections.title: The business context matters
sections.body: A request must use the signed-in user’s active business and permissions. Client-supplied business IDs cannot be used as a shortcut to another business’s records.

sections.title: Read-only by default
sections.body: The assistant boundary is designed for read-only summaries. Creating or changing invoices, stock, payments and customer messages is outside this release’s AI permissions.

sections.title: Honest availability
sections.body: An optional read-only model adapter is implemented. It needs an explicitly configured provider and credentials; live provider quality remains unverified. Recorded-data summaries remain available without it.

business-types.title: A workspace for different kinds of shops
business-types.description: Explore grocery, hardware, vegetable and mobile accessory workflows in DukaanSet, plus clear limitations for specialised business modules.
business-types.headline:
Different shops.
A familiar foundation.
business-types.intro: Your business category changes the useful units, examples and everyday attention. Core sales, inventory and customer records stay connected across the platform.

sections.title: Kirana and grocery
sections.body: Manage packaged and loose items with a product catalogue, low-stock and product-expiry attention, and customer credit. Batch-specific expiry automation is a later phase.

sections.title: Hardware and electrical
sections.body: Use pieces and metres to make products understandable. Supplier purchases and customer balances sit alongside sales. Configured pack sizes support stock receipt conversions; advanced selling conversion matrices are planned.

sections.title: Fruit and vegetable shops
sections.body: Use decimal weight quantities, edit current product prices and record wastage through an explained stock adjustment. Existing invoices retain their original prices. True offline billing and weighing-scale integrations are not active.

sections.title: Mobile, clothing and mixed shops
sections.body: Start with the shared item catalogue, descriptive variations and piece-based stock. Full size/colour matrices, serial and warranty tracking are planned. A general category keeps the core workflow available to mixed businesses.

business-types/grocery.title: Kirana and grocery shop workspace
business-types/grocery.description: A connected grocery workflow for packaged and loose products, daily billing, low-stock attention and customer credit in DukaanSet.
business-types/grocery.headline:
Your everyday essentials.
Neatly in place.
business-types/grocery.intro: From the morning milk rush to the last packet of atta. Keep your bills, everyday stock and customer udhaar together.

sections.title: Packets and loose items, side by side
sections.body: Give each item a clear unit. A packet of atta can sell as a piece; loose dal can sell by kilogram. Product names and units help you confirm the right item at the counter.

sections.title: A purchase should reach your shelf
sections.body: Record stock received from a supplier and see its quantity added to inventory. When an item sells, the confirmed bill records the corresponding deduction.

sections.title: Keep regular-customer credit visible
sections.body: Attach a partial-payment sale to the right customer and review their balance later. The sale amount and the cash received remain distinct.

sections.title: Expiry attention and remaining limits
sections.body: Save a product expiry date to see approaching-expiry attention. Batch numbers, batch-specific expiry rotation and integrated barcode-scanner workflows still need dedicated implementation.

business-types/hardware.title: Hardware and electrical stock workspace
business-types/hardware.description: Manage hardware catalogue units, stock, supplier purchases and customer credit with the shared DukaanSet business workflow.
business-types/hardware.headline:
Every metre. Every piece.
A clearer record.
business-types/hardware.intro: Pipes, wires and fasteners have different units. Give each product the right measure and follow customer credit alongside sales.

sections.title: Make the item recognisable
sections.body: Use a specific product name and the correct unit: a ¾-inch pipe by piece, copper wire by metre or a fastener by piece. Descriptive catalogue entries reduce ambiguity at the counter.

sections.title: Follow orders into stock
sections.body: Supplier purchase records add received quantities. A stock ledger records where a change came from, while low-stock attention helps you decide what to reorder.

sections.title: Keep customer balances connected
sections.body: Link contractor or regular-customer credit to actual bills and record later repayments. The balance stays inside the selected business.

sections.title: Configured packs and remaining limits
sections.body: Save the number of base units in a pack before receiving stock in boxes or packs. Unknown pack sizes are rejected. Advanced selling conversion matrices, job-site allocations and purchase orders remain planned.

business-types/vegetables.title: Fruit and vegetable billing workspace
business-types/vegetables.description: Use weight-based product quantities, current price editing and wastage adjustments for fruit and vegetable shops in DukaanSet.
business-types/vegetables.headline:
Fresh stock.
A clear daily picture.
business-types/vegetables.intro: Sell by the kilogram, update today's product prices and record wastage so remaining stock stays understandable.

sections.title: Sell the weight you actually measured
sections.body: A quantity such as 0.750 kg is a normal sale. Use decimal quantities and a per-unit selling price, with financial totals calculated and checked on the server.

sections.title: Prices change; old bills do not
sections.body: Edit a product's current selling price as your rates change. Confirmed invoices retain the price recorded at the time of sale, so their historical totals remain understandable. A dedicated daily-rate history is a later phase.

sections.title: Give wastage a reason
sections.body: Record damaged or spoiled produce as a negative stock adjustment with a clear explanation. The change appears in stock history instead of becoming an unexplained quantity loss.

sections.title: Connected weighing is a future integration
sections.body: No weighing-scale hardware integration is active. Bills require network access to confirm. Advanced offline sales and stock reconciliation remain a dedicated later phase.

business-types/mobile.title: Mobile accessories shop workspace
business-types/mobile.description: Start mobile accessory billing, catalogue stock and purchase tracking in DukaanSet. Dedicated serial-number and warranty capabilities are planned.
business-types/mobile.headline:
A small accessory.
A complete picture.
business-types/mobile.intro: Keep accessories easy to find, create itemised bills and track what is selling. Advanced device tracking is a later release.
business-types/mobile.note: Serial numbers, device repair tickets and warranty tracking are planned, not active capabilities.

sections.title: Keep accessories easy to find
sections.body: Use descriptive names for cables, covers and screen protectors. Piece-based quantities and product prices make the shared sales flow useful for everyday accessory transactions.

sections.title: Record the sale and the shelf
sections.body: Confirm an itemised bill to record its payment and reduce stock. View invoice history when a customer needs a copy of the sale.

sections.title: Review what to restock
sections.body: Set a minimum-stock level for fast-moving essentials and record supplier purchases when new items arrive.

sections.title: Device-specific work needs more
sections.body: IMEI or serial tracking, warranty terms, device repair, service tickets and size/colour variants need dedicated workflows. Do not use descriptive product names as a substitute for those required records.

pricing.title: DukaanSet plan structure and pricing status
pricing.description: Review proposed Trial, Starter and AI Pro plans. DukaanSet commercial pricing is being finalised; no subscription payment collection is active.
pricing.headline:
Your everyday essentials.
Room to grow.
pricing.intro: Trial, Starter and AI Pro are proposed plan categories. Commercial prices, usage limits and the availability of provider-dependent tools will be published before a paid launch.
pricing.note: Pricing is being finalised. There is no subscription checkout or payment collection in this release.

sections.title: What happens today
sections.body: You can explore a fictional demo or create a business in the configured development installation. These actions do not buy a subscription or create a paid commercial agreement.

sections.title: What will be published before launch
sections.body: Each commercial plan will need its price, billing period, applicable taxes, usage limits, support scope, cancellation terms and provider-dependent functionality explained together.

sections.title: AI needs its own limits
sections.body: An AI Pro label is a roadmap proposal, not a guarantee of unlimited model usage. The provider, quotas and failure behaviour must be configured and validated before a commercial AI service is offered.

how-it-works.title: Getting started with DukaanSet
how-it-works.description: Learn the DukaanSet setup flow: create an account, choose a business and language, add products, create a bill and review your day.
how-it-works.headline:
A little setup.
A clearer everyday flow.
how-it-works.intro: Start with the essentials you know. Add business details as you need them. Your first confirmed sale should show how billing, stock and customer payments belong together.

sections.title: 01 · Create your account
sections.body: Use your name, email and password to create an account. The current authentication flow uses passwords; it does not claim to send SMS OTPs or recovery email without a provider.

sections.title: 02 · Choose your business
sections.body: Give the business a name, choose a primary category and select English, Hindi or Hinglish. Extra profile details can follow later.

sections.title: 03 · Add the products you sell
sections.body: Start with a few real items: name, unit, selling price, cost and opening stock. Check that the quantities reflect what is actually on your shelf.

sections.title: 04 · Make and review a bill
sections.body: Add products and quantities, then record the payment. Choose a customer if any amount remains due. Review the total before confirming.

sections.title: 05 · Read your day
sections.body: See the confirmed sale on the dashboard, review the stock change and check the customer’s balance if it was a credit sale. Finish with a daily closing summary.

help.title: DukaanSet help centre
help.description: Practical help for account setup, bills, stock, customer credit, business switching, demo data and DukaanSet’s current offline limitations.
help.headline:
A clear next step
when you need one.
help.intro: Start with these practical guides. If a workflow fails, preserve what you entered, read the message and retry only after checking whether the record was saved.

sections.title: I am opening the app for the first time
sections.body: Choose the demo for fictional examples, or register for a fresh account. Finish business setup, add a product with stock and create a small test bill you can identify clearly. The demo is separate from your real records.

sections.title: My bill did not save
sections.body: Check your connection and the inline error. A quantity must be positive, stock must be available and a credit sale needs a customer. Do not assume a failed confirmation created an invoice; review bill history before retrying.

sections.title: My customer paid later
sections.body: Open the customer record and record a repayment for the amount actually received. Confirm the payment method and date. A repayment changes the balance and collections, not the original sale total.

sections.title: I switched businesses
sections.body: The active business controls the dashboard, catalogue, customers and reports. Check the selected shop before entering records. If your session expires, sign in again before continuing.

sections.title: I am offline or AI is unavailable
sections.body: Online confirmation is required for financial records. The offline page is a safe fallback, not an offline database. Live AI is not connected in this build and needs a tested provider adapter plus credentials. The core records remain available without it.

sections.title: I need to report a problem
sections.body: Use the project’s GitHub issue tracker. Include the page, the action and the error text, but omit passwords, customer phone numbers and financial exports. Support response times are not yet defined.

contact.title: Contact the DukaanSet project
contact.description: Report DukaanSet issues and product feedback through the project GitHub repository. Commercial support channels are not established yet.
contact.headline:
Tell us where
the day got harder.
contact.intro: Useful feedback starts with what you were trying to do. The project’s GitHub issue tracker is the available channel for development feedback and reproducible bugs.
contact.note: A commercial support desk, support email, phone number and response-time commitment have not been established.

sections.title: Report an issue
sections.body: Describe the page, what you expected, what happened and whether it happens again. Device type, browser version and the exact error text can help reproduce a problem.

sections.title: Share a workflow suggestion
sections.body: Tell us the shop type and the real task: weighing produce, collecting a partial payment, receiving a supplier delivery or closing the day. Avoid publishing customer or supplier records.

sections.title: Keep private information private
sections.body: GitHub issues are public. Never post passwords, session cookies, identity documents, customer contact details or full business data exports. A dedicated private support channel must be established before commercial operation.

about.title: About DukaanSet
about.description: DukaanSet is an in-development business management product for Indian small shops, built around connected daily workflows and clear implementation status.
about.headline:
The shop comes first.
The software follows.
about.intro: DukaanSet is a working product for the daily rhythm of small businesses: sell an item, update the shelf, remember the payment and understand the day.

sections.title: The problem we are working on
sections.body: Separate notebooks, stock lists and payment records make the same transaction feel like several jobs. A connected flow can reduce repeated entry and make the result easier to understand.

sections.title: Our product principles
sections.body: Use familiar words. Keep the next action clear. Ask for fewer details up front. Build for phones. Calculate and validate business records on the server. Show what is unavailable instead of simulating success.

sections.title: A product in development
sections.body: The current build connects a first set of everyday shop workflows. Merchant usability research, production infrastructure, operational security review, tax review and provider integrations must continue before a commercial launch.

sections.title: Brand and company status
sections.body: DukaanSet is the selected working product name. This site does not claim a registered company identity, trademark clearance, a physical office or an established customer base. Domain and trademark clearance remain launch work.

privacy.title: Privacy policy draft — legal review required
privacy.description: A review-required DukaanSet privacy draft describing intended data categories, business separation and unresolved retention and launch policy details.
privacy.headline:
Your business data
deserves clear answers.
privacy.intro: This is a development draft, not a final privacy policy or a compliance certification. A qualified review and an identified service operator are required before commercial launch.
privacy.note: DRAFT · Legal review required. Do not treat this page as a completed privacy compliance statement.

sections.title: Data the application uses
sections.body: Account information includes name, email and a hashed password. Business records may include shop details, products, stock movements, customers, suppliers, invoices and payments. Enter only the contact details you need for a legitimate business record.

sections.title: How the core records are used
sections.body: The application uses records for authentication, the selected business’s workflows, summaries and exports. Authorisation is checked by business. A configured AI provider, if later enabled, must be assessed for the specific data sent to it.

sections.title: Providers and hosting
sections.body: Hosting, database, email, analytics and AI providers depend on the actual deployment configuration. A final policy must name the operator, explain relevant processors and disclose any cross-border handling. No advertising or analytics consent claim is made by this draft.

sections.title: Retention and requests
sections.body: Retention periods, deletion procedures, data access handling, grievance contact and backup expiry are not finalised. Business export alone is not a complete deletion or privacy-rights process. These controls must be completed before a live service handles real customer records.

sections.title: Before using real data
sections.body: Review the deployed service’s final privacy notice and security controls. Do not enter unnecessary identity documents, payment card details, UPI PINs, banking passwords or sensitive personal information.

terms.title: Terms of service draft — legal review required
terms.description: A review-required DukaanSet terms draft. Commercial operator identity, pricing, service terms, liability and jurisdiction require finalisation before launch.
terms.headline:
Clear expectations.
Before a real launch.
terms.intro: These are proposed development terms, not a final commercial agreement. Operator identity, paid-plan terms, liability and applicable dispute provisions need legal review.
terms.note: DRAFT · Legal review required. A completed commercial agreement is not available in this release.

sections.title: Intended use
sections.body: DukaanSet is intended to help authorised users maintain their own business records. Users must enter accurate data, protect account access and use the service lawfully. A demo is fictional and should not be used as a real financial record.

sections.title: Financial records and integrations
sections.body: The service records data you enter. Payment-method labels do not initiate bank or UPI transfers. Ordinary invoices are not government-verified GST e-invoices. AI examples are not professional tax, accounting or legal advice.

sections.title: Development limitations
sections.body: This build is under development. Production availability, backup recovery, support levels and specialised business features need separate verification. Maintain appropriate copies of essential business records.

sections.title: Subscriptions and termination
sections.body: Prices, billing periods, cancellations, refunds, account suspension and data access after termination are not finalised. No subscription checkout exists in this release.

sections.title: Legal details still required
sections.body: The responsible service operator, contact details, applicable law, dispute handling and reasonable liability provisions must be defined and reviewed before users enter into a paid commercial relationship.

security.title: DukaanSet security approach and release boundaries
security.description: Understand DukaanSet’s authentication, business data isolation and current security boundaries, including production hosting, backups and provider review.
security.headline:
Business records.
Clear boundaries.
security.intro: Security is part of the transaction flow: authenticate the user, resolve their business, validate the input and commit a consistent record. This page describes intent and release boundaries without claiming certification.

sections.title: Authentication and business isolation
sections.body: The application uses password-based authentication and server-issued sessions. Data operations are scoped to an authorised business. Switching a business must also switch its records and permissions.

sections.title: Financial changes are checked on the server
sections.body: The server validates quantities, prices, stock availability and payment constraints. Related invoice, inventory and customer-balance changes belong in one transaction so a partial update does not appear as a completed sale.

sections.title: Private routes and safe offline behaviour
sections.body: App pages require a session and are excluded from indexing. The service worker caches only the offline notice and public brand assets. It does not cache authenticated pages, financial API responses or customer data.

sections.title: Secrets and provider boundaries
sections.body: Provider credentials belong in server environment variables. Payment collection, messaging and AI require their own configured integrations. The app never asks for UPI PINs, banking passwords or card information.

sections.title: Production readiness requires more
sections.body: Deployment-specific HTTPS, access controls, rate-limit storage, monitoring, restore drills, data retention and an independent security review remain necessary. This release does not claim SOC 2, ISO certification or legal compliance.

faqs.question: Can I use DukaanSet on my phone?
faqs.answer: Yes. The app supports phones, tablets and desktops. HTTPS installation is available; offline billing is not.

faqs.question: How do stock and customer dues update?
faqs.answer: Confirmation records the sale, stock and payment in one transaction. Credit requires a customer.

faqs.question: Will demo data enter my business?
faqs.answer: No. Demo shops are isolated and fictional. Your own business records stay separate.

faqs.question: Are UPI transfers verified?
faqs.answer: UPI receipts are manually recorded. Bank verification and subscription checkout are not connected.
